SHARES ITS PEOPLE: REVOLVING DOOR, BOARD SEATS, FORUM MEMBERS (CENTRAL BANK OF BOLIVIA (BOLIVIA))

Source says: Central Bank of Bolivia (Bolivia). Banco de Cochabamba S.A. employed an official of the Central Bank of Bolivia (Bolivia) before or after their time there. Jaime Valencia Valencia (General Manager, Banco Central de Bolivia, 1996-2006 and again from 16 January 2020): from Banco de la Union S.A. to General Manager of the Banco Central de Bolivia (no dates given for the bank post). Valencia's CV on the Banco Central de Bolivia's own site names three financial employers with no titles and no dates: Banco de la Union S.A., Banco de Cochabamba S.A. and Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A. The ownership of one of the three is now stated, and it points the other way: the English Wikipedia article on Banco Union says the Bolivian government 'established a new public financial entity called Banco de la Union S.A.' by public deed on 28 July 1979 and that 'Through the National Treasury, the government established a 97% stake in the new bank', describing it as a Bolivian state bank. On that statement the Banco de la Union leg is a public-sector move. Because the CV gives no dates, it cannot be excluded that he was there in a period of different ownership. The other two employers are still unsettled: ASFI's 1999 annual report lists 'Banco de Cochabamba S.A. en Liquidacion' under the heading 'ENTIDADES EN LIQUIDACION', which is a status and not an ownership statement, and nothing opened this round states the ownership of Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A. Banco Union (Wikipedia)

Baghdad, Iraq

1 central bank tied to it.

OTHER TIES: NAMED IN A CASE, PRINTS ITS MONEY, AUDITS OR MANAGES FUNDS (CENTRAL BANK OF IRAQ (IRAQ))

Source says: Central Bank of Iraq (Iraq). The Central Bank of Iraq vault, Baghdad holds gold reserves belonging to the Central Bank of Iraq (Iraq). The Central Bank of Iraq's 2025 financial statements split the holding into three lines in note 4: gold reserve abroad, gold reserve at the CBI vault and gold coins at the CBI vault. Only the bank's own vault is named; the note names no institution for the much larger holding held abroad, so that part is recorded as a blank rather than guessed at. Central Bank of Iraq, Financial Statements for the year ended 31 December 2025, note 4 'Gold reserve and gold revaluation reserve'
